label: Intermediate
blurb: The vocabulary of getting things done — the offices you have to visit, the paperwork you get handed, and the words that come up when you talk to parents.
blurbZh: 把事情辦好會用到的詞彙：各處室、要簽要交的文件，以及跟家長溝通時聽到的說法。

questions.q: A homeroom teacher asks you to write a note in a student's 聯絡簿. This is —
questions.why: 聯絡簿 (liánluòbù) goes home in the schoolbag every day. Teachers write homework and short notes in it; parents sign to confirm they've read it.

questions.q: The office asks if you can 代課 tomorrow morning. They want you to —
questions.why: 代課 (dàikè) = to substitute-teach. The person doing it is a 代課老師 (dàikè lǎoshī), a substitute teacher.

questions.q: You need to be away on Friday. You tell the office 我禮拜五要—
questions.why: 請假 (qǐngjià) = to request leave. Common types: 病假 (bìngjià) sick leave, 事假 (shìjià) personal leave, 公假 (gōngjià) official leave.

questions.q: Questions about your timetable and textbooks are handled by the —
questions.why: 教務處 (jiàowùchù) = academic affairs — timetables, textbooks, exams. 學務處 handles student life, 總務處 the building and budget.

questions.q: A student has a discipline or safety issue. The office that handles it is —
questions.why: 學務處 (xuéwùchù) = student affairs — discipline, health, clubs, safety. It is the office you'll deal with most outside your own classes.

questions.q: You're invited to a 班親會 on Friday evening. This is —
opts: a parent–teacher meeting for one class
questions.why: 班親會 (bānqīnhuì) is the class-level parent meeting run by the homeroom teacher. FETs are often asked to say a few words.

questions.q: A colleague says 下禮拜段考. Next week there will be —
questions.why: 段考 (duànkǎo) is the periodic term exam — usually two or three per semester. 期末考 (qímòkǎo) is the final one.

questions.q: The calendar marks next Monday as 補假. This means —
opts: a make-up day off for a holiday you worked
questions.why: 補假 (bǔjià) is the compensating day off. Its partner is 補班 (bǔbān) — a Saturday you have to work to bridge a long weekend.

questions.q: A student proudly says they are this week's 值日生. They are —
opts: the student on duty for classroom chores
a hall monitor for the whole school
the top scorer on the last exam
questions.why: 值日生 (zhírìshēng) is the student on rotating duty — wiping the board, turning off lights, fetching the lunch cart.

questions.q: The 家長會 is sponsoring the sports day prizes. This group is —
questions.why: 家長會 (jiāzhǎnghuì) is the school-wide parent association. Don't confuse it with 班親會, the meeting for a single class.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your colleague is telling you that on Saturday there is —
questions.why: 研習 (yánxí) = an in-service training session or workshop. Teachers must accumulate 研習時數 (yánxí shíshù), training hours, each year.

questions.q: A teacher asks 我們調課好嗎？They are proposing to —
opts: swap class periods with each other
questions.why: 調課 (tiáokè) = to swap or reschedule periods between teachers. Different from 代課 (dàikè), where someone covers for you.

questions.q: You need to interrupt two colleagues who are talking. You open with —
questions.why: 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) works as 'excuse me' and as a light apology. It is softer than 對不起, which is a real apology.

questions.q: You tell the office 我要影印三十份. You need —
questions.why: 影印 (yǐngyìn) = to photocopy; 份 (fèn) is the measure word for copies or sets. The machine itself is the 影印機 (yǐngyìnjī).

questions.q: Your colleague says 我今天有四節課. The measure word 節 is counting —
questions.why: 節 (jié) counts class periods: 一節課 = one period. For classes as groups use 班 (bān), and for people use 位 (wèi) politely.

questions.q: Parents refer to you as their child's 導師. This word means —
questions.why: 導師 (dǎoshī), often shortened to 班導 (bāndǎo), is the homeroom teacher responsible for one class's daily life.

questions.q: The newsletter says 校慶 is next month. The school is preparing for —
questions.why: 校慶 (xiàoqìng) is the founding anniversary — usually a big day with performances, sports, and alumni visiting.

questions.q: You are asked to prepare a 學習單 for your lesson. This is —
opts: a lesson plan for the principal
questions.why: 學習單 (xuéxídān) is the worksheet students fill in during or after an activity. 教案 (jiào'àn) is the lesson plan itself.

questions.q: A clerk hands you a form and says 麻煩您核章. They need you to —
opts: sign or stamp it to approve it
questions.why: 核章 (hézhāng) = to sign off with your seal or signature. Taiwanese paperwork moves by collecting 章 (zhāng), personal stamps, down a chain.

questions.q: Staff start discussing 期末 preparations. They mean —
opts: the start of a new school year
questions.why: 期末 (qímò) = end of term, with 期末考 (finals) and 結業式 (jiéyèshì, closing ceremony). Its opposite is 期初 (qíchū).

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. At three o'clock in the meeting room there will be —
questions.why: 開會 (kāihuì) = to hold a meeting. 會議室 (huìyìshì) is the meeting room; the weekly staff meeting is 校務會議 (xiàowù huìyì).

questions.q: A student who missed the exam will have a 補考. This is —
questions.why: 補考 (bǔkǎo) = make-up exam. The 補 (bǔ) prefix means 'to make up' — you'll also meet 補課 (make-up class) and 補假 (make-up day off).

questions.q: Someone says 今天有兩位家長來. Why 位 rather than 個?
opts: 位 is only used for numbers over ten
位 is the polite measure word for people
位 means the parents are seated
questions.why: 位 (wèi) is the respectful measure word for people — 一位老師, 兩位家長. 個 (gè) is neutral and can sound blunt for guests.

questions.q: You tell the class 我們來分組. You are asking them to —
questions.why: 分組 (fēnzǔ) = to divide into groups; a group is a 組 (zǔ). 小組討論 (xiǎozǔ tǎolùn) is group discussion.

questions.q: You need five more minutes before going to the office. You say —
opts: 我先下班了 (wǒ xiān xiàbān le)
我等一下再過去 (wǒ děng yíxià zài guòqù)
questions.why: 等一下 (děng yíxià) = in a moment / hold on. 我等一下再過去 means 'I'll come over in a bit' — polite and very common.

questions.q: A student is struggling emotionally. The office that supports them is the —
questions.why: 輔導室 (fǔdǎoshì) is the counselling office. If you notice a student in difficulty, telling the 導師 and 輔導室 is the right first step.

questions.q: The schedule shows 防災演練 on Wednesday. You should expect —
questions.why: 防災演練 (fángzāi yǎnliàn) = disaster drill. In Taiwan this usually means 地震 (dìzhèn, earthquake) — duck, cover, hold, then evacuate to the playground.

questions.q: A student says they joined 熱舞社 this semester. 社 here refers to —
questions.why: 社 (shè) is short for 社團 (shètuán), a student club. 熱舞社 is the street-dance club; 英語社 would be the English club.

questions.q: A colleague ends a request with 拜託你了. The tone is —
opts: warm and pleading — 'I'm counting on you'
questions.why: 拜託 (bàituō) = please / I'm counting on you. Among colleagues it's friendly; it is stronger and warmer than 麻煩你.

questions.q: Parents will receive the 成績單 at the end of term. This is —
questions.why: 成績單 (chéngjīdān) = report card or transcript. 成績 (chéngjī) alone means grades or results.
